detail noun

also in detail, details, go into detail, go into a matter

classical

Verg. A. 8.618: oculōs per singula volvit
Quint. 6.1.12: īre per singula (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 302
Traupman 303

singula, singulōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

the details, each particular

The neuter plural of singulī, one by one: per singula, in detail; rem per singula inīre, go into a matter in detail (Traupman 302).

Other words

  • singillātim — one by one, in detail

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.143: singillātim potius quam generātim (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. detail: in detail; Traupman 302; Traupman 303

    Also singulātim, and in many manuscripts sigillātim (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • explērī nequit atque oculōs per singula volvit

    he cannot look his fill, and runs his eyes over every detailVerg. A. 8.618

  • Rem enim tōtam per cēnam per singula inībō.

    I’ll go into the whole matter in detail over dinner.Traupman 91

  • rem per singula inīre

    to go into a matter in detailTraupman 303

  • rem inīre

    to go into a matterTraupman 322

See also describe, explain, example.
